summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Gombrich earned his BA and DPhil at Oxford and studied under Kenneth Roy Norman, Walpola Rahula, and Gananath Obeyesekere. He served as Oxford's Boden Professor and directed the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies.
Hartshorne studied at Princeton and the University of Chicago. He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Minnesota (~1924–1940) and the University of Wisconsin–Madison (~1940–1970).

Hauschild specialized in Indology and linguistics, studying at Tübingen, Leipzig, and Jena under Albert Debrunner and Johannes Hertel. He held posts as Lektor at the University of Jena and as a member of the Saxon Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

A linguist, Henebry studied at St. Patrick's Pontifical University, St. John's College, Waterford, and the University of Freiburg. He also studied at the University of Greifswald under Heinrich Zimmer from ~1896 to ~1898.

Robinson worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees at the University of Alberta, SOAS, and the University of London under Arthur Waley, David Friedman, David Llewellyn Snellgrove, and Edward Conze. He held posts at Toronto and Wisconsin–Madison.

Seager works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1987), later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College (~1994).

Davidson studied at New York University and Harvard University. He held positions at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1987, 1996, and served as a professor of psychology there from 2001 to 2017.
A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Kohn completed his PhD in 1988 at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, where he studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Payne specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, having studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and was on the faculty at the Graduate Theological Union and Chicago.
Sprigg was a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology who studied at Oakham School. He held academic posts at SOAS and the University of London from ~1948 to ~1980.

A scholar of religious studies and history, Kieckhefer studied at Saint Louis University, UT Austin, and Monumenta Germaniae Historica. He joined Northwestern University in 1975 and served as president of the American Society of Church History and Societas Magica.

Working in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, King studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster under Daniel Mariau. He held academic posts at Stirling, Vanderbilt, and the University of Glasgow, and edited the Numen Book Series.
Eaton is an Indologist and historian who studied at the College of Wooster (~1958–1962). In ~1972, he became a Professor of History at the University of Arizona.
Working in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, Jaffe held academic posts at North Carolina State University (~1994–2000) and Duke University (~2000).

Mahoney is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, completing his Master of Arts in 2002 while also holding an affiliation there in 2001.

Working in linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Morris studied at Battersea. He served as headmaster at the Royal Masonic School for Boys, lectured at King's College School, was master at Dedham Grammar School, and presided over the Philological Society.

Boyle completed graduate work at the University of Washington and studied under Kyozan Joshu Sasaki. He held teaching posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, and the University of New Mexico.

Hayes specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, Shoryu Katsura, and T. Venkatacharya, later holding posts at Toronto, McGill, Leiden, and the University of New Mexico.
Hottelet was an affiliate of the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1971, where he studied Buddhist studies under Narayan Hemandas Samtani.
Spiers was a scholar in history and archaeology who completed his education at King's College London (~1856–1858) and the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts (~1858–1861).
